title: P31 reversed: RoPE base 10000 -> 500 so most rotary pairs complete a full turn within pretraining lengths
description: P31 reversed: every block of the 051-claude incumbent uses RoPE base 500 instead of 10000, kept through RL and eval, with no other change. Pretraining sees at most 516-token records but expert iteration must sample 7-14 line proofs, so fewer rotary pairs with unseen phase angles at those longer distances should make round-1 samples on long targets valid more often, giving expert iteration more correct long proofs to train on.
hypothesis: At base 10000 only 8 of 16 rotary pairs per head complete a full turn within the longest pretraining record, so attention scores at the longer query-key distances of >=7-line proofs rely on phase angles the low-frequency pairs never saw; Liu et al. 2023 (Scaling Laws of RoPE-based Extrapolation) find a small base such as 500 extrapolates better after training at a fixed length because more pairs are fully trained. Prior runs that reduced positional resolution all scored below their incumbents (029 base 1e5: 129 vs 148; 041 half the pairs unrotated: 253 vs 270; 058 NoPE in block 3: 263 vs 286), so the untested opposite direction, more high-frequency pairs, is the natural next test of whether positional encoding limits length transfer.
expected_delta: Central +0 to +20 dev-transfer solves at true length >=7 versus incumbent 051-claude mean 286.33 (288/260/311); downside -30 if coarser long-range position information hurts retrieval of distant lines. Val loss within +-0.004 of 051 (0.0923 on seed 0); pretraining updates within 3% of 051 (2320 on seed 0); per-seed total secs within +5% of 051 (1053 on seed 0), under the 1200 s cap. If it helps, expect higher round-1 RL sample acc on >=7-line targets than 051.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) with RoPE base 500 (LowBaseRopeGPT subclass in pretrain.py)
arch.change: one mechanism: rope_cache(..., base=500.0) instead of the fork default base 10000, in every block, during pretraining, RL and eval. Pair i of each 32-dim head has wavelength 2*pi*500^(i/16) = 6.3 ... 2133 tokens (was 6.3 ... 35330). Depth 5, width 256, 8 heads, d_ff 1024, init and all optimizer/schedule/data settings unchanged from 051-claude.

rope.pairs_completing_a_turn_within_516_token: 12 of 16 (wavelengths <= 451) vs 8 of 16 (<= 353) at base 10000; 516 = longest pretraining record
rope.source: Liu et al. 2023, Scaling Laws of RoPE-based Extrapolation (arXiv 2310.05209): smaller bases let more rotary dimensions see a full period during training

arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: state dict is exactly the fork GPT's, but the forward must use base 500: LowBaseRopeGPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from pretrain.py. The harness keeps the returned module object through RL and eval.
arch.kv_cache: fork Block and per-block cache dicts unchanged; only cos/sin tables differ. CPU check with the sampler's mask convention (causal prefill of 30 tokens, then 10 single-token cached steps): max |logit diff| vs full forward 9.5e-7 (fork GPT same test: 1.0e-6).

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) are in Muon. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Muon lr*0.01 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent per-update shrinkage at every schedule fraction, including the former finish window; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Fork default construction with 5 blocks (LowBaseRopeGPT adds no modules, so RNG draws are identical to 051), then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter after moving to device. Gain = 0.02 * sqrt(max(rows, columns)); exact element second moment 0.0004. Embedding and readout keep the fork's normal(0.02) draws; biases zero; LayerNorm weight 1 and bias 0. No reinitialization during RL.
config.timing: no extra compute (cos/sin tables are the same size); expect ~2300 updates in 300 s and total secs ~950-1060 like 051 (1053 on seed 0)
